Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `testIterateDOM()` calls `doTestIterate(DocumentContainer.MODEL_DOM)`. Within `doTestIterate`, the test sets up a JXPathContext with a single namespace prefix "a" mapped to the namespace URI "ns". The test then asserts iteration over XPath pointers for "/a:doc/a:elem" expecting two elements with the paths "/a:doc[1]/a:elem[1]" and "/a:doc[1]/a:elem[2]".

The bug report states a problem with `JXPathContext.iteratePointers()` when multiple prefixes map to the same namespace URI. The example XML has elements "a:elem" and "b:elem" sharing the same "ns" URI but different prefixes. Iteration returns the first element twice, missing the second.

The relevant method `JXPathContext.iteratePointers(String xpath)` is abstract, implemented in `JXPathContextReferenceImpl`. Its implementation calls `compileExpression(xpath)` and then uses the compiled expression to iterate pointers in `iteratePointers(String xpath, Expression expr)`.

The root cause is likely in how namespace prefixes and their mappings are resolved during XPath compilation or evaluation, particularly when multiple prefixes correspond to the same namespace URI. The system probably caches or matches based on prefixes alone or does not correctly handle multiple prefix aliases for the same namespace URI, causing pointer iteration to omit some elements or produce duplicates.

This diagnostic aligns with the described symptoms: iteration over elements with different prefixes is malfunctioning due to incomplete or incorrect namespace prefix to URI mapping handling in the iteratePointers evaluation path.

Recent bug reports about NamespaceResolver mapping issues suggest changes to prefix-URI cache or mapping behavior are related, reinforcing that namespace multiple prefix handling is the source of this bug.

Hence, the bug occurs due to improper handling of multiple prefixes for the same namespace URI in pointer iteration implementation within `JXPathContextReferenceImpl.iteratePointers` and the underlying namespace resolution in XPath evaluation. The test fails because the iteration returns duplicated elements for the first prefix and misses elements for the second prefix sharing the same namespace URI.

This diagnosis directs focus to methods involved in namespace resolution during XPath evaluation and pointer iteration, especially in classes like `JXPathContextReferenceImpl` and possibly `NamespaceResolver`.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
